title: SQL Injection Prevention
description: Never concatenate or format user input directly into SQL queries. Always use parameterized queries or ORM bind variables to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Prevention
description: Always sanitize and HTML-escape user-supplied data before rendering it in web views, responses, or email templates.

title: No Hardcoded Secrets or API Keys
description: Never commit plaintext credentials, passwords, JWT secrets, private keys, or API tokens directly in source code. Retrieve them from environment variables or a secure key vault.

title: Path Traversal and File Path Validation
description: Validate and resolve user-controlled file paths against a trusted base directory to prevent directory traversal attacks (e.g., ../../etc/passwd).
bad_example: with open(os.path.join('/uploads', user_filename), 'rb') as f: return f.read()

title: Cryptographically Secure Random Generation
description: Use cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generators (e.g., secrets module) rather than standard random for security tokens, passwords, or salts.

title: Boundary Condition and Off-by-One Handling
description: Check boundary limits in loop conditions, array slicing, and pagination logic to prevent off-by-one errors and IndexOutOfBounds exceptions.

title: Null / None Defensive Checking
description: Always check for None or null before accessing object attributes or calling methods on optional return values.
good_example: user = find_user(user_id); return user.profile.email if user and user.profile else None

title: Mutable Default Arguments in Function Signatures
description: Never use mutable data types (e.g. lists, dicts) as default parameter values in function definitions in Python, as they persist across function calls.
bad_example: def append_item(item, target_list=[]): target_list.append(item); return target_list
good_example: def append_item(item, target_list=None): if target_list is None: target_list = []; target_list.append(item); return target_list

title: Exception Handling Specificity and Preservation
description: Avoid catching bare Exception or pass blocks without logging. Catch specific exceptions and preserve tracebacks or log error context.
good_example: try: do_work() except (IOError, ValueError) as e: logger.error('Work failed: %s', e); raise

title: Deterministic Resource Cleanup and Context Managers
description: Always use context managers (with statements or try-finally) when handling files, network sockets, or database connections to avoid resource leakage.
good_example: with open('data.txt', 'r') as f: content = f.read()

title: Avoid N+1 Database Query Anti-pattern
description: Avoid executing individual database queries inside a loop. Use eager loading, joined loads, or bulk fetch with IN operators.
bad_example: for order in orders: customer = db.query(Customer).get(order.customer_id)

title: Efficient String Concatenation and Memory Usage
description: Avoid repeated string concatenation in loops with the + operator. Use list appending and str.join() or string buffers for O(n) memory allocation.
bad_example: res = ''; for s in large_strings: res += s

title: Cyclomatic Complexity Control
description: Keep method cyclomatic complexity under 10. Split large, deeply nested control structures into modular helper functions for testability.
bad_example: def handle_process(): # 6 levels of nested if/for loops and 300 LOC

title: Comprehensive Unit Test Coverage for PRs
description: Every Pull Request introducing new business logic or bug fixes must include corresponding automated unit tests covering both happy and edge cases.
bad_example: # PR changes payment logic in 5 files with 0 tests added
good_example: # PR includes tests/test_payment.py covering success, failed payment, and timeout scenarios

title: Documentation and Type Annotations
description: Public APIs, service methods, and exported interfaces must include clear docstrings and typing annotations describing inputs, outputs, and raised errors.
bad_example: def calculate(a, b): return a * 0.15 + b
good_example: def calculate_tax(subtotal: float, rate: float = 0.15) -> float: '''Calculate tax amount based on subtotal.''' return subtotal * rate
